prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1126; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss was received from the policyholder reporting a collision in a parking lot while the vehicle was parked. The driver was listed as a household member of the policyholder, so coverage for this driver is confirmed.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. Photos taken at the scene show damage consistent with the impact described, and the other driver gave an account that matches the claimant's.

Entry 3: Witness statements were obtained and all of them describe the collision as the claimant reported it. The claimant has been represented by counsel since early in the claim, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 4: A neighbor mentioned in a brief call that the vehicle appeared to have been damaged a few weeks before the reported collision. The neighbor could not give specifics, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in our file or in the prior claims search.

Entry 5: The vehicle was inspected and the repair estimate lines up with the damage pattern from the reported impact. The claimant's knee injury was reported and medical records show it fits the kind and force of the crash, with no earlier injury to that body area on record. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the file is being reviewed against the usual recovery timeline.

Entry 6: The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation with the adjuster and through counsel. Based on the police report, witness statements, photos and the inspection, the file is being prepared for the next review step, with the neighbor's comment noted for follow-up.
